questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: One of the most crucial aspects in choosing my study destination was the strong school spirit and campus culture in the United States. This sense of community and engagement among students was something I found very appealing and quite different from what I was used to. Additionally, I was highly motivated by the opportunity to experience a different education system. Studying in the U.S. allowed me to explore a new approach to university life, including different teaching methods, classroom dynamics, and student involvement, which I found both exciting and academically enriching.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. In Madison, there was an International Student Center where I could go in person to ask questions and get help, which made the transition much smoother. Additionally, they were very responsive via email, so it was always easy to get assistance whenever I needed it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived at my study destination, I received helpful support from the International Student Center. I had some questions regarding my visa, so I went there in person and received clear and useful assistance. In addition, they offered a city and campus tour together with other exchange students. This helped me become familiar with the area and easily locate the buildings where I would have my classes, which made the start of my studies much easier.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult to find off-campus housing, mainly because most places only offer one-year leases rather than short-term options such as five months. In addition, off-campus housing is relatively expensive. My main recommendation would be to start searching as early as possible to increase the chances of finding suitable accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus can be a great experience, as the facilities are generally very good, at least where I lived. However, future exchange students should be aware that it can also be quite expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process took some time to understand at first. It was not immediately clear where to find information about the available courses, and since the system was different from what I was used to, it took some time to navigate and make sure I was registering correctly. However, once I became familiar with the system, the registration process worked well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help was mainly available via email. They were good at responding to questions, although it was important to keep the time difference in mind when waiting for replies.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful in registering for the classes I wanted, as I was able to enroll in all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice to future exchange students would be to be patient and allow some time to understand the registration system, as it may be different from what you are used to. It is also a good idea to carefully read the available information and not hesitate to contact the staff via email if you have any questions. Once you become familiar with the system, the registration process works well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was appropriate and well-structured. However, the teaching and learning approach was quite different from what I was used to, so it took some time to adjust. The workload was manageable, while still being academically challenging and rewarding. Overall, the courses met my expectations and provided a good balance between theory and practical application.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching at my host institution was quite different from that at UCPH. There was a much stronger focus on student interaction and participation in class. In addition, there was more continuous assessment, such as quizzes after almost every class or at least on a weekly basis, which required students to stay consistently engaged and organized.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend COMARTS345: Online Communication & Personal Relationships and COMARTS200: Introduction to Digital Communication. Both courses had excellent instructors and teaching assistants who were very engaging and supportive. The course content was interesting, and the teaching style made the classes both engaging and educational, which created a very positive learning experience.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: While not entirely unexpected, both insurance and housing turned out to be more expensive than I had anticipated. These costs were higher than expected and became a significant part of my overall expenses.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and food that I cooked myself were more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many cultural, athletic, and social activities available for students. A wide range of sports events, such as football games, ice hockey, and volleyball matches, were especially popular and created a great atmosphere on campus. In addition, the International Student Office was very good at bringing exchange students together by organizing various social events, which made it easy to meet new people and feel part of the community.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend attending sports events. They are a very American experience and a lot of fun, and they offer a great opportunity to experience the strong school spirit and sense of community on campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend exploring the city and seeing what is going on, especially on weekends. Spending time with American friends is also a great way to experience the local culture. In addition, it can be fun to take trips around the city and discover what it has to offer, as there is always something new to see or do.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to adjust to the local culture at my exchange site.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My main tip would be to be open and not be afraid to take initiative and approach people. In addition, joining different clubs or student organizations at the university is a great way to meet new people and socialize with local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One cultural difference I found challenging was the tipping culture, as this is quite different from what I was used to. Additionally, it took some time to adjust to the fact that class attendance was mandatory and that there were more weekly academic requirements compared to the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I especially appreciated the strong school spirit and the feeling of being part of a large and engaged community. You could really feel that people value the social aspect of university life, for example through the strong sense of togetherness at sports events.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: First, be open and proactive when it comes to socializing. Taking initiative and joining clubs or attending events makes it much easier to meet people and feel part of the community. Second, be prepared for a different academic system with mandatory attendance and continuous assessments such as quizzes and weekly assignments. Staying organized from the beginning is very important. Finally, plan your finances carefully, as housing, insurance, and daily expenses can be more expensive than expected.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: One useful thing for future exchange students to know is that planning ahead makes a big difference, especially when it comes to housing and finances. It is also important to be aware of the time difference when communicating with staff via email.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was being part of the strong campus community and school spirit, while also experiencing a different academic system and way of university life. It was both personally and academically enriching and gave me valuable new perspectives.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was definitely housing and visa-related matters. The visa process was especially challenging because parts of it were shut down over the summer just before my departure, which made the situation more stressful and difficult to manage.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
